_README: licensing-policy.json — THE machine-readable source of truth for which parts of
Correlix are Apache-2.0 core and which are commercial add-ons.
Three consumers read this file and nothing else:
1. scripts/gen-licensing-map.py  renders LICENSING.md at both repository roots.
2. scripts/licensing-gate.py     enforces checks A-H (SPDX headers, notice files,
3. tests/test_licensing_consistency.py  fails the build on any drift between this
file, the rendered map, and every place the
Editing prose in LICENSING.md instead of editing this file changes nothing that is
enforced. Edit here, then run:  python3 scripts/gen-licensing-map.py --write
FAIL-CLOSED: an unclassified top-level directory, an unknown SPDX identifier, or a
file marked commercial outside a commercial path is an ERROR, never a warning.
DEFAULT-OPEN: anything this policy does not name is Apache-2.0. Isolation, safety
and correctness properties are never commercial.
canonical_sentence: Correlix core is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. Commercial add-on modules are licensed under the Correlix Enterprise License (LicenseRef-Correlix-Enterprise) — see LICENSING.md.

locked_commercial_set._why: The ONLY entitlements the owner has locked as commercial (2026-09-04). Everything else in the tiering plan is a proposal and is NOT gated. A capability may not be marked commercial here without appearing in this list.

Team.what: The security-findings lane: normalized findings, exposures, the findings API and its retention.

Enterprise.what: Device-hardening dialects beyond the default set, and compliance frameworks beyond the default two.
Export of findings/evidence to an external SIEM.
MSP / org-hierarchy MANAGEMENT of many tenants. Explicitly NOT tenant isolation.

core_is_never_commercial._why: Stated positively so that a future change that tries to paywall one of these fails review on sight. These are safety and product-identity properties.
items: Tenant and organisation ISOLATION, including the Postgres FORCE-RLS policies, chTenantScope, osTenantFilter and every per-tenant store filter. Isolation is a safety property, never a paywall.
Discovery, collection and multi-protocol telemetry ingestion.
The telemetry pipeline, event bus and storage bootstraps.
The correlation engine and RCA: verdicts, causality paths, seams, evidence classes.
The investigation and troubleshooting surface, including protocol diagnostics.
BGP public-data views (looking glass, RPKI, AS-path graph, geofeed).
Local authentication and OIDC single sign-on.
The licence mechanism itself and the community ceilings/limits enforcement, so a Community operator can read and verify exactly what limits them.

excluded_paths._why: Directory names never classified and never scanned, anywhere in the tree. Each is generated, vendored, or local state — none of it is Correlix source whose licence we declare. The consistency test derives its exclusion list from THIS array, so adding a build directory means adding it here with a reason.

entries.reason: The two licence texts the SPDX identifiers resolve to. The directory itself is part of the open declaration and is readable by everyone.
Compose stack, Dockerfiles, nginx/vector/storage configuration. Deployment machinery for the whole product; nothing tier-gated lives here.
Design records, runbooks, audits and the tracker. Documentation of the open product, including the design of the commercial split itself.
Docusaurus customer documentation site. Ships in the frontend image; documents every tier.
Installer, watchdog, preflight, release and audit tooling. Operators must be able to read, run and modify everything that touches their host.

Backend, frontend, correlation engine and configuration. Apache-2.0 by default; the commercial add-ons listed under commercial_paths and mixed_directories live inside this tree and are marked individually.
entries.mixed_note: Commercial code inside src/ is marked file-by-file and directory-by-directory. Only src/backend/internal/ldap is cleanly separated today.

entries.reason: The telemetry field catalogue and its fixtures. A data contract every tier depends on.
Repository-level pytest suites, including this licensing gate. Tests of commercial code stay Apache-2.0 so anyone can verify the product's claims.

repo_root_entries._why: Top-level entries of the OUTER repository root that belong to this project. The outer root is a thin wrapper: it carries CI, the shared guardrails file and the licence declaration, and the project itself in a nested directory of the same name.

not_part_of_this_project.why: An unrelated project sharing the working directory. CLAUDE.md declares it out of scope; Correlix declares no licence over it.
A stray 58-byte text file from an unrelated macOS application. Not source; not ours to license.

commercial_paths._why: Directories that are CLEANLY commercial today: every file in them implements a locked commercial entitlement and nothing else. Each gets a LICENSE notice file and an SPDX header on every source file. A directory that merely CONTAINS some commercial code does not belong here — it belongs in mixed_directories.

entries.reason: The whole package is LDAP/Active-Directory directory authentication: the bind and search client, its TLS posture and its configuration domain. Nothing in it serves local auth or OIDC, which stay core. Verified 2026-09-04: 4 files, no core caller other than the package-main wiring seam.

mixed_directories._why: Directories that MIX Apache-2.0 core code with code implementing a locked commercial entitlement. They stay Apache-2.0 in full until the commercial part is extracted, because over-claiming commercial on a shared package would wrongly restrict core code. Each names what must move and where. Tracked by TRACKER.md row 237.

entries.core_part: The hardening rule catalogue, engine, benchmark provenance and configuration parsing. Community runs hardening and exposure for its device ceiling.
entries.commercial_part: dialect_fabric.go — the Arista EOS and Nokia SR Linux data-centre-fabric dialects; multi-vendor dialects beyond the default set.
entries.why_not_split_today: The dialects register into the same catalogue and rule types as the core engine; separating them needs a dialect-registry seam, which is code movement this change is forbidden from doing.

entries.core_part: The projection engine and the default two frameworks (NIST 800-53 and CIS v8), which Community gets.
entries.commercial_part: Framework definitions beyond the default two (HIPAA, PCI, CSF).
entries.why_not_split_today: Frameworks are rows in one projection table, not separable files. Splitting needs a framework-registry seam.

entries.core_part: Nothing core depends on this package, but the findings it serves include the hardening and exposure findings Community is entitled to.
entries.commercial_part: The findings lane as a paid entitlement, the framework enablement surface, and the (unbuilt) SIEM export route.
entries.why_not_split_today: The Community and Team findings surfaces are the same routes with different ceilings. Separation is a licence-gate question, not a file-move, until the gate exists.

entries.core_part: The normalized finding model, which the core compliance checks produce into.
entries.commercial_part: The findings lane as a paid entitlement.
entries.why_not_split_today: The model is the contract between a core producer and a commercial consumer. It most likely stays Apache-2.0 permanently; recorded here so the decision is explicit rather than assumed.

entries.commercial_part: The security evidence lane as a paid entitlement.
entries.why_not_split_today: Same as secapi: a ceiling question, not a file boundary.

entries.core_part: Tenant ISOLATION, the tenant store, the collection and routing scope. Core forever, explicitly never commercial.
entries.commercial_part: org.go and governance.go — the organisation hierarchy above tenants and its governance registry, which is the MSP fleet-management surface.
entries.why_not_split_today: Org isolation is DERIVED from tenant isolation (reachesTenant bounds cross-org reach), so the org type is load-bearing for a core safety property. Extraction must keep the isolation half in core, which is a genuine design task.

header_enforcement._why: How check A is scoped TODAY. Stamping an Apache-2.0 header into ~2350 source files is a mechanical sweep that would collide with every branch in flight; it is scheduled, not skipped. What is enforced now is the direction that can actually go wrong: a commercial marking in the wrong place, or a commercial path missing its marking.
rules: Every source file under a commercial_paths entry MUST carry the commercial SPDX identifier.
No file outside a commercial_paths entry may carry the commercial SPDX identifier.
Any file that carries an SPDX identifier at all MUST carry the one its path maps to.
Unknown SPDX identifiers anywhere are an error.

pending.what: Repo-wide `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` headers on core source.
pending.why_deferred: A ~2350-file mechanical diff across backend, frontend and correlation would conflict with every concurrent branch. LICENSE, LICENSING.md and the per-directory notices already make the licence of every file determinable today; the headers make it determinable per file in isolation.

import_boundary._why: Check E. Apache-2.0 core must never depend on commercially licensed code: a core-only build has to remain buildable and shippable, and an Apache-2.0 file that cannot compile without a commercial package is Apache-2.0 in name only.
import_boundary.rule: No package outside commercial_paths may import a package inside commercial_paths, except the assembly-layer allowances below.

assembly_allowances.why: Package main is the assembly layer: it wires optional features together and is where a licence gate switches one on or off. Wiring is not a core dependency; the wiring file is the seam that gets a build tag when ee/ extraction lands.

artifact_requirements._why: Check H. A licence declaration that does not reach the customer is not a licence declaration. Every artifact Correlix ships must carry the notice files.

container_images._why: Check D. Dockerfiles that build a CORRELIX image must declare the licence in OCI metadata. Dockerfiles that only repackage a third-party image (adding no Correlix source) must NOT: labelling someone else's software with our licence would be a false claim. Every Dockerfile in the tree is classified here exactly once; a new one that nobody classified fails the test.

ours.why: Builds the Go API from src/backend.
Builds the correlation engine from src/correlation.
Bakes the built SPA and docs portal into nginx.
Same image, building the SPA inside Docker.
Copies the Correlix cloud poller modules.
Builds the Correlix mock NMS from repository source.
Builds the Correlix mock ServiceNow from repository source.
Ships the Correlix sealing entrypoint and seal handler.
Builds the Correlix lab traffic generator from repository source.

third_party_repackage.why: Prepares the stock nginx image to run non-root. Contains no Correlix source; the configuration is bind-mounted at runtime.
Trims and flattens the stock OpenSearch image. The content is OpenSearch, not Correlix.
Adds curl to the pinned stock Vector image. The content is Vector (MPL-2.0), not Correlix; labelling it Apache-2.0 would be false.
An Ubuntu toolchain container used to build VM images. Contains no Correlix source and is never shipped.
A stock python image with pip requirements for the lab twin. Contains no Correlix source and is never shipped.

release_blockers._why: Conditions under which `scripts/licensing-gate.py --release` fails. These are things that must not reach a customer, as distinct from the everyday drift the default mode catches.

entries.what: LICENSES/Correlix-Enterprise.txt still contains the marker CORRELIX-ENTERPRISE-TEXT-PLACEHOLDER.
entries.why: Files are marked LicenseRef-Correlix-Enterprise but the identifier resolves to no terms. Shipping code under a licence that does not exist grants nothing and is not honest.
entries.owner_action: Obtain the drafted Correlix Enterprise License from counsel and replace the placeholder.

entries.what: CONTRIBUTING.md states the CLA requirement but names no signing process.
entries.why: Open core depends on holding the rights to relicense contributed code into the commercial edition. A stated-but-unsigned CLA does not confer those rights, and inventing a process or a URL would be worse than saying it is undecided.
entries.owner_action: Choose the mechanism (CLA assistant on the repository, or a countersigned document) and record it in CONTRIBUTING.md.
